correctness.rationale: For every 0<r<=2 with epsilon=1, the explicit continuous three-piece F_r has F_r(0)=0, F_r(r)=(0,r+1), and F_r(t)/t tends to (1,0) at both infinities. The six ordered interval pairs exhaust every s<t; exact lower and upper Euclidean norm inequalities are derived in RESULT.md. Key positivity uses a=(r-1)_+, a<=1, monotonicity of sqrt(r)+1/sqrt(r)-1+1/r on [1,2], and 1-u+u/r>=2-r>=0. Scaling yields every epsilon. The universal upper bound follows from the 2epsilon longitudinal projection estimate and the origin-distance inequality. The large-radius branch is precisely published Turnšek Theorem 1.3 and the origin value follows from f(0)=0. Supplementary CHECK.py reproduced 400000 sampled pair checks; sampling is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Turnšek’s full text Remark 2.1 explicitly identifies the unanswered attainment question for 0<r<2epsilon. His upper theorem and >=2epsilon extremizers do not imply the missing lower branch. The new piecewise explicit construction achieves equality for each radius in that interval. Šemrl (2025) contains the canonical Hilbert isometry and weaker inequalities, not the pointwise equality. Targeted published-finding corpus and literature searches returned no equivalent; bibliographic uncertainty persists.

value.rationale: This resolves the explicitly stated nontrivial sharpness question in Turnšek (2026), Remark 2.1, by supplying the exact short-radius lower bound through a universal continuous low-dimensional geometric construction. It completes the sharp pointwise defect profile from zero to all positive radii, exposes a nonuniform jump of the envelope at the origin despite f(0)=0 for every map, and separates universal pointwise attainability from a common all-radius extremizer. The new part is not a numerical improvement obtained by renaming or direct substitution.
